1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __and the at least one BMC polypeptide is expressed from a heterologous polynucleotide__.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme __that is heterologous to the cell__.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes __that are heterologous to the cell__.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __and is heterologous to the cell__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and is heterologous to the cell__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __that are heterologous to the cell__.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species __and are heterologous to the cell__.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons __and are heterologous to the cell__.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __and is heterologous to the cell__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide __for the purpose of engineering a metabolic function in the host cell__.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a different bacterial species__.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a non-Enterobacteriaceae species__.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a non-E. coli species__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a non-Shewanellaceae species__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial species__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial species__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial species__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial species__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one heterologous bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product __wherein the at least one enzyme is heterologous to the cell__; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __for the purpose of producing the product in a compartmentalized manner__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __and the substrate is not naturally metabolized by the host cell__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __and the substrate is not naturally metabolized by the host cell__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __and the substrate is not naturally metabolized by the host cell__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and the enzyme is heterologous to the cell__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __wherein the compartments are isolated based on expression of a heterologous BMC polypeptide__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment comprises at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide__.
